title: Count interventions mechanically: record every resume and every hand commit
description:
ncv's acceptance says to count interventions and report the number. Nothing records them. The close-out had to RECONSTRUCT the count from checkpoint history and the first-parent log: 17 stops, 9 hand commits on the integration branch, 33 hand triages.

A number that has to be reconstructed can be argued with, and the Phase 4 gate's rule is 'one intervention is failure' — so the number decides the verdict.

Work:
- Record each resume in .ticfac/: who, when, and which stop it followed.
- Flag every integration-branch commit that came neither from an attempt merge nor from the run itself. Those are the hand commits, and on ncv I made nine of them.
- Record each triage with its actor (the finding record already carries 'by'; count it).
- Report the three numbers in the close-out, from the records, with no inference.

From ncv close-out finding 4a76698a.
acceptance_criteria: The close-out reports resumes, hand commits and hand triages from recorded data, and each number can be traced to the records that produced it
